title: Blindly Mapping Value Objects as Normalized Entities (ORM Join Table Abuse)
damaged_code:
```xml
<!-- Mapping a collection of Value Objects as a database Entity in ORM -->
<set name="groupMembers" table="tbl_group_member">
    <key column="group_id"/>
    <composite-element class="GroupMember">
        <property name="name" column="name"/>
    </composite-element>
</set>
```
pattern: Mapping a small collection of domain Value Objects (e.g., a set of contact phone numbers or group members) to a separate database table using join tables with foreign keys.
why_bad: Unnecessary database normalization. It forces expensive `JOIN` queries to fetch basic values that are always read together with the parent aggregate, introduces database-level locks, and prevents columns from being `NULL` in certain set operations [242, 528].
detection: ORM mappings representing lightweight Value Objects (non-identifiable types) inside dedicated database tables with foreign keys.
counterexample: Mapping a collection of rich, independently mutable entities to separate tables.
fix: Denormalize the Value Objects directly into the parent table's columns (e.g., using serialized formats or flat columns).
